questions.q: Why does the role redesign create `meridian_itil_base` and have other roles extend it with `contains_roles`, instead of just deleting the three duplicate roles?
options: Deleting roles is not technically possible on the Now Platform
It gives the next access request a role to reuse instead of inventing a new near-duplicate — the actual fix for sprawl, not just cleanup
contains_roles is required for any role to function at all
Base roles automatically expire after one year
questions.explain: A legible hierarchy with a reusable base role is what stops the next request from creating yet another overlapping role.

questions.q: What makes the new `annual_income` ACL script stronger than simply requiring a single dedicated role with no script?
options: It also checks that a standard underwriter is actually assigned to that customer's case, while still letting senior underwriters view any customer's data
It removes the field from the customer table entirely
It disables the field for every role, including senior underwriters
It only runs during business hours
questions.explain: The scripted condition adds a real relationship check (case assignment) on top of the role requirement — least privilege beyond a static role gate.

questions.q: In the Okta SSO migration plan, why is MFA enforced at the Okta policy level rather than configured separately inside ServiceNow?
options: ServiceNow does not support any form of MFA
Because once authentication happens through Okta via SAML, Meridian's existing mandatory MFA policy — already enforced for every other app — applies automatically
MFA must always be configured per-application, never centrally
Okta cannot enforce MFA for SAML-based applications
questions.explain: Routing authentication through the existing enterprise IdP means the existing enterprise MFA policy carries over without separate configuration.

questions.q: Why does the migration plan keep exactly one local break-glass admin account instead of leaving local authentication fully enabled for everyone?
options: Local authentication must always stay enabled for all users by platform default
Break-glass accounts are required by the SAML 2.0 specification
Okta cannot be configured without a local fallback for every user
One tightly monitored account covers the real need (an SSO outage) without leaving the weak local-auth path open for 1,800 users
questions.explain: A single monitored break-glass account handles the legitimate outage scenario without reintroducing the authentication-debt finding at scale.

questions.q: What does deactivating (rather than deleting) `itil_l2_temp`, `itil_l2_temp_v2`, and `incident_approver_backup` preserve?
options: Nothing — deactivating and deleting a role have identical effects
The roles' sys_audit history, consistent with this course's governance and audit-trail practices
The ability for new users to still be assigned those old roles
The original ACLs that referenced those role names
questions.explain: Deactivating keeps the historical record intact for audit purposes, rather than erasing evidence of what access existed and when.
